name: Six Senses Fort Barwana
positioning: Six Senses Fort Barwara: a converted 14th-century Rajasthani fort with two palaces and two temples within its walls
best_for: Travelers who want to stay inside a restored historic Rajasthani fort
Wellness seekers interested in Ayurveda-based programs

facts.text: The resort is a 14th-century fort converted into a Six Senses sanctuary of well-being.
The fort was originally owned by a Rajasthani Royal Family.
The conservation effort incorporates two palaces and two temples within the walled fort.
The fort faces the Chauth ka Barwara Mandir temple and has a view of the lake.
Each suite is designed in a contemporary Rajasthani style, subtly incorporating high tech and artwork.
Suites have private terraces with views toward the Barwara Heritage village or the Chauth ka Barwara Mandir temple above the lake.
Wellness combines the preventative principles of Ayurveda with Western influences.
Three restaurants serve Rajasthani-inspired fresh, sustainable cuisine.
The landscaping integrates purely endemic plants and water features.
The property works with the local community to rewild the forests to the east and revive the sacred lake.

highlights.text: A 14th-century fort, once owned by a Rajasthani Royal Family, converted into a Six Senses sanctuary of well-being.
Two palaces and two temples are preserved within the walled fort.
Suites in contemporary Rajasthani style have private terraces looking toward the heritage village or the Chauth ka Barwara Mandir temple above the lake.
Wellness blends the preventative principles of Ayurveda with Western influences.

considerations.text: The setting is rural Rajasthan, with the fort's palace domes rising from agricultural fields and rugged wilderness.
WhataHotel notes the remote rural location requires planning.
